ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 2 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Gwen Ifill

code.originalText: Biopsy result: endometrial cancer; staging CT, gynecologic oncology consultation, Lynch syndrome tumor screening, and preparation for surgery

text.paragraph: Endometrial biopsy result and gynecologic oncology consultation. [S]

Ms. Ifill returns two weeks after her first visit. The transvaginal ultrasound two days after that visit showed a 16 mm heterogeneous endometrium with internal blood flow and two small fibroids. The endometrial biopsy taken at the first visit, telephoned to her four days later, shows endometrioid adenocarcinoma, FIGO grade 2, with loss of MLH1 and PMS2 staining and a wild-type p53 pattern. CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis the next week showed an enlarged right external iliac lymph node and an enlarged left para-aortic node, with no disease in the liver, lungs, bones or peritoneum. Dr. Delacroix of gynecologic oncology saw her this morning. The bleeding has lessened to occasional spotting. She has no pain, bowel or bladder change, leg swelling or weight loss. She says she is shaken but glad the answer came quickly, and wants to keep working through treatment if she can. She has had no thoughts of self-harm. [S]

list.item:
Endometrioid adenocarcinoma of the endometrium, FIGO grade 2, mismatch repair deficient (C54.1). Endometrial cancer diagnosed four days after her first visit, because the bleeding was sampled at once and the ultrasound was done the same week. The enlarged pelvic and para-aortic nodes on CT suggest stage III disease, which surgery will settle. Dr. Delacroix recommends minimally invasive hysterectomy with removal of both tubes and ovaries, sentinel node mapping and removal of the enlarged nodes in two weeks; treatment after surgery will depend on the final stage and the molecular class. The loss of MLH1 and PMS2 is the universal Lynch syndrome screen; MLH1 promoter methylation testing has been sent on the biopsy to tell an acquired change from an inherited one. CA-125 28 U/mL is normal and will not be used for follow-up. Fit for surgery: albumin 4.1 g/dL, creatinine 0.80 mg/dL. [S]
Surgery with Dr. Delacroix in two weeks.
MLH1 promoter methylation on the biopsy; POLE sequencing on the surgical specimen.
Hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV tests drawn today, in case systemic treatment follows.
Genetic counseling once the methylation result is back.

Postmenopausal bleeding (N95.0). Explained by the diagnosis made today; superseded. [S]
Problem resolved.

Call for heavy bleeding, fever, or leg swelling. Next scheduled visit 2026-02-24: review three weeks after surgical staging: final pathology and molecular class, genetic counseling, and the first cycle of dostarlimab with carboplatin and paclitaxel.
